notes:
VERDICT RATIONALE: the declared 200 schema ({success, error}) is honestly small and every response observed fit it exactly — no missing/undeclared keys anywhere. DRIFT is scored against the capability's own GUIDANCE PROSE, not its JSON schema: the guidance claims sending the TR-NNN string 'fails upstream rather than being rejected here' — implying an error of some kind. What actually happened (attempt 1) was a plain HTTP 200 {"success": true} that changed NOTHING, verified by two independent re-reads immediately after. That is a THIRD, previously undocumented failure mode for this capability, worse than the one the guidance already warns about ({success:false, error:'Please check test runs'} for a missing/non-array test_runs): a wrong-typed-but-present array element produces a 200 that LIES about having succeeded, with no error key at all to distinguish it from a genuine unlink. A caller who does not independently re-read the plan after this call would believe the unlink happened and would have no way to know otherwise.

QUESTION 1 (the one that matters most) — DOES UNLINKING DELETE THE RUN? NO, DEFINITIVELY. get_test_run_by_integer_id(17578623) returned a full 200 test_run object immediately after the real unlink (attempt 2): same identifier TR-9111, same test_cases_count (1), same name, only test_plans emptied and updated_at bumped. The run was NOT deleted — it survives as an orphaned, plan-less run, exactly as this capability's own intent text promises ('Detach test runs from a test plan without deleting them'). This capability's mode classification (write, not destructive) is THEREFORE CORRECT for TR-9111's case: there is no hidden destructive side effect routing around the destructive-tier gate. This is a clean, reassuring answer, not a defect.

QUESTION 2 — THE list_test_runs_by_integer_id test_plans[] READER BUG, FINAL PIECE: before the unlink (setup steps 3+4), get_test_run_by_integer_id and list_test_plan_test_runs_by_integer_id both correctly showed TR-9111 linked to TP-1632, while list_test_runs_by_integer_id (same run, same instant, include_test_plan=true) showed test_plans:[]. After the real unlink (attempt 2), list_test_runs_by_integer_id was re-read (p=1) and STILL shows TR-9111's test_plans:[] — but now that value is actually TRUE, since the run really is unlinked. Because the field reads [] in BOTH the genuinely-linked and genuinely-unlinked states, with zero observable difference between them, this confirms what the task suspected: list_test_runs_by_integer_id's test_plans field does not merely return stale data, it NEVER populates at all, regardless of the real underlying state. list_test_plan_test_runs_by_integer_id and get_test_run_by_integer_id both correctly flip from populated to [] across the same write — two independent working readers, one broken reader, all observed on the identical run across the identical change.

QUESTION 3 — ID FORM: the capability's guidance insists on the integer uuid and warns the TR-NNN string 'fails upstream.' Empirically it does NOT fail upstream — it returns a clean 200 success and silently no-ops (see attempt 1 above). Only the bare integer uuid (17578623) actually performs the unlink. This directly answers the task's 'which id form is demanded' question: the integer is required for the write to take effect, but the wrong form is not rejected — it is silently absorbed with a false-positive success, which is arguably worse than 'failing upstream' as documented.

QUESTION 4 — PUT-VS-PATCH / ADDITIVE-VS-REPLACE: NOT INFERRED, per the task's explicit instruction, because TP-1632 had exactly one linked run (TR-9111) and no way existed to test partial unlinking against a multi-run plan without touching TP-1616 (explicitly off-limits). No claim is made here about whether unlink is additive-vs-replace for a list of run ids; only the single-run case was exercised.

QUESTION 5 — test_runs_count ON THE PLAN: updated correctly. get_test_plan_by_integer_id(48319) went from test_runs_count/total_test_runs_count {active:1,closed:0} to {active:0,closed:0} immediately after the real unlink, matching list_test_plan_test_runs_by_integer_id's row count exactly (0 rows). No count-vs-rows desync observed on this capability's own effect.

QUESTION 6 — BAD-ID TEST (run id not linked to this plan): attempt 3 sent TR-9061's uuid (17574995, a run genuinely linked to a DIFFERENT plan, TP-1616/48283) as if unlinking it from TP-1632/48319. Result: 200 {"success": true}, absorbed silently — exactly matching this capability's own guidance ('ids that were never linked to this plan... are absorbed silently'). Verified TP-1616 was NOT touched: get_test_plan_by_integer_id(48283) updated_at is still 2026-09-18T12:53:05.000Z, byte-identical to its established fixture baseline; TR-9061 remains linked via list_test_plan_test_runs_by_integer_id(48283); sub_plans_count still 14. So unlike attempt 1's lying-success-that-does-nothing-when-it-should-have-worked, this is a lying-success-that-correctly-does-nothing-because-there-was-nothing-to-do — the SAME response shape ({success:true}, no distinguishing field) covers both a genuine unlink, a wrong-id-form no-op, and a not-linked-here no-op. All three are indistinguishable from the response alone; only independent re-reads separate them.

SCOPE / SAFETY: only TP-1632 (48319) and TR-9111 (17578623) were mutated. TP-1616 (48283) and TR-9061 (17574995) were read four times total across this probe and never written to; both are confirmed byte-identical to their pre-probe baselines. TR-9111 now sits unlinked from any test plan, per the task's expectation that it is expendable and disposable. Entitlement-gated 200 {success:false} and error-envelope drift were not observed/exercised — no 4xx/5xx was produced by any of the three attempts, so those two watch items remain unverified for this capability specifically.
